summary: Gottfried Kinkel studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1831 to 1834. Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held posts at the University of Bonn (~1837–1848) and ETH Zurich (~1866–1882).

Gotthilf Heinrich von Schubert studied at the Universities of Leipzig (~1799–1801) and Jena (~1801–1803). Working in philosophy and other fields, he held posts at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1819–1827) and the University of Munich (~1827–1853).

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner studied at King's College London and Heidelberg University. Active in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held posts at King's College London, Government College University, Lahore, University of the Punjab, and Oriental Institute, Woking.
Gouriswar Bhattacharya was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts as a Lehrbeauftragter at the Free University of Berlin, attested in 2007 and 2026.

Govind Chandra Pande studied under Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya (~1943–1947). Active in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he served at the Universities of Allahabad and Rajasthan, Banaras Hindu University, Allahabad Museum, and the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye studied at Bahauddin College, Elphinstone College, and Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon. A scholar of Indology and sociology, he headed the Department of Sociology at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959).

Govind Swamirao Gai worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India (attested 1958–1966), Chief Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), and consultant for AIIS (attested 1986).

Govind Vinayak Devasthali, who worked in Indology and linguistics, studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944). He held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts & RYK Science College (attested 1944) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).
Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indology scholar who held positions as Professor (attested 1933–1939) and Director (attested 1953–1957) at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.

Grace S. Fong studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia. A scholar in Sinology, she served as a professor at Smith College (~1985–1989) and as associate professor and department chair at McGill University (~1990).

Graeme MacQueen studied at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1974–1979). Working in Buddhist studies and religious studies, he was a lecturer at McMaster University from circa 1977 to 2013.

Grafton Elliot Smith studied at the University of Sydney, Sydney Medical School, and St John's College. Active in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held a post at University College London from circa 1919 to 1936.
Graham E. Clarke worked in Tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and as a Senior Member at the University of Oxford (attested 1998).
Graham Lock is a scholar in linguistics and Buddhist studies who studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Priest studied at Cambridge and the London School of Economics under John Lane Bell, and earned a D.Litt at Melbourne. Active in philosophy and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Melbourne, St Andrews, and CUNY.
Grant V. Aston, a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies, completed a PhD in philosophy at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), studying under Jack Copeland and Paul Harrison.

Graves Chamney Haughton studied at Fort William College. Active in Indology and linguistics, he was Professor of Hindú Literature and the History of Asia at East India Company College (1819–1827) and secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Gray Tuttle earned his PhD at Harvard University in 2002. Specializing in Tibetology, Sinology, and history and archaeology, he has held professorial posts at Columbia University, attested between 2008 and 2026.

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902 and founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873.
Greg Bailey is an Indology scholar who studied under J. Durham and Madeleine Biardeau. He held posts, including Professor, at La Trobe University (attested 1994 and 2004).
